title: Root Zone Temperature (RZT) Dynamics, Dissolved Oxygen (DO) Saturation, and ATP Yield in NFT Spinach Channels
author: Dr. vmffkxhs2362
abstract: High root zone temperature (RZT > 22°C) reduces dissolved oxygen (DO) solubility in Nutrient Film Technique (NFT) channels, causing root hypoxia and Pythium vulnerability in spinach. We modeled root respiration rates and ATP yield across RZT regimes from 14°C to 24°C. Chilling nutrient solution to 18°C maintained DO saturation above 7.8 mg/L and prevented anaerobic ethanol fermentation.
key_findings: Root respiration rate peaked at 20°C (12.4 μmol O₂/g DW/h) while DO solubility dropped below 6.5 mg/L at 24°C.
Maintaining solution RZT at 18°C increased root ATP production by 38.6% compared to 24°C.
Pythium ultimum root colonization was reduced by 85% at RZT 18°C under continuous DO oxygenation.
